ai.description: This frog reaches 5–7 cm. It is brown or yellowish with dark dorsal markings and a white belly. Key features include large, adhesive toe pads and a distinct dark stripe running from the snout to the eye.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Polypedates himalayensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-bordered white spot in the center of its tympanum, a feature absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Polypedates himalayensis* inhabits moist subtropical and temperate broadleaf forests across the Himalayas, typically at elevations ranging from 1,000 to 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Himalayan Tree Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for insects among the foliage of its humid, high-altitude forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Polypedates himalayensis* breeds during the monsoon, laying foam nests containing 100–200 eggs on vegetation overhanging water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Himalayan Tree Frog inhabits the northeastern Indian states of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, and Meghalaya, typically at elevations between 500 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Himalayan Tree Frog produces a series of rapid, high-pitched "tink-tink" notes, typically heard emanating from vegetation near stagnant pools or forest streams.
